title: Put a centre-pinch lens cap back on a DSLR's kit lens and stand the camera down
instruction: Put the lens cap back on the camera and leave the camera standing on the table.
context: Capping the lens is the last thing done before a camera goes back in its bag: it keeps dust, fingerprints and scratches off the front element. Entry-level DSLR kits such as the Canon EOS 2000D (Rebel T7) with the EF-S 18-55mm lens ship with a centre-pinch cap (Canon E-58 II): two tabs on its front, when pinched, pull two sprung latches in so the cap passes the lip of the lens's 58 mm filter thread; let go, the latches spring out behind the lip and the cap holds. People do it with two hands: one holds the camera up by its body, the other pinches the cap and presses it square onto the lens. A cap pushed on crooked or let go before it is flat on the face does not latch and falls off later. The lens points sideways a few centimetres above the table, so the camera has to be lifted to present the lens, and held while the cap is pressed on, then set back down on its base.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) A Canon EOS 2000D (Rebel T7) body with its kit lens, the EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 IS II, standing on its base, lens pointing toward -y (toward the right arm), lens axis at x 340 mm and 44 mm above the table (est), the lens's front face at y -30 mm. Body 129 x 101.3 x 77.6 mm (published), black; pentaprism hump on top 58 mm across x and 46 mm deep (est), hand grip on the camera's right (world -x). Lens 68.5 mm across and 70 mm long (published), 58 mm filter thread. Camera with lens, battery and card 0.675 kg (published: body 475 g, lens 200 g). The lens's front, standing for its filter thread: a lip 1.5 mm deep, 56 mm across inside, behind it a groove 60 mm across and 7.5 mm deep (est; a real 58 x 0.75 mm thread is shallower, crests about 57.2 mm and root 58 mm across, see fidelity). (2) Its front cap, a Canon E-58 II centre-pinch cap, black, lying face up at x 250 mm, y -130 mm: front plate 62 mm across and 2.5 mm thick, 12 g (est). On its front two finger tabs 24 mm long and 10 mm high, outer faces 38 mm apart (est). Each tab is one part with a latch tooth on the cap's back; it slides 2.5 mm in against a 2 N spring (est). Pinched fully, both teeth clear the lip; let go, each tooth springs out behind the lip, its flat catch face overlapping the lip's rear face by 1.4 mm. Two fixed lugs at 90 degrees to the latches centre the cap in the lip with about 1 mm of play. Teeth and lugs reach 6 mm behind the cap's seat face, with lead-in ramps; the cap lies on them. Nothing else is on the table. Both grippers start open at the ready pose. Friction (est): camera 0.6, cap 0.45.
scoring: End state, read from the poses of the camera and the cap, the two latch slides and both grippers. Cap home: the cap's seat face within 1 mm of the lens's front face (and not more than 0.5 mm past it), the cap's centre within 2 mm of the lens's axis, its axis within 3 degrees of the lens's; its turn about its own axis does not matter. Real trial: a 1 mm feeler does not enter between the cap and the lens's rim at four points 90 degrees apart, and the lens rim showing beyond the cap differs by no more than 4 mm between opposite sides. Latched: home with BOTH latches out, each within 0.4 mm of its rest position (a latch that is not behind the lip is held in by the lip). Real trial: hold one tab in and turn the camera lens down over a towel for 3 s, the cap stays on; repeat with the other tab. Camera down: the camera's up axis within 10 degrees of vertical and its lowest point within 5 mm of the table top. Real trial: a phone level on the top plate and a look along the table. Fell: latched for the rest of the trial if the camera's or the cap's lowest point goes more than 30 mm below the table top (off the table). Let go and still: over the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones stay 30 mm or more from the camera and the cap, and neither part moves more than 5 mm or turns more than 5 degrees. Score, held 1 s at the end: 0 if Fell, if not let go and still, or if the cap is not home. 1.0 cap latched and camera down. 0.5 cap latched, camera not down (on its side or back). 0.25 cap home but a latch not out, camera down. 0 for anything else.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; the camera is boxes and a cylinder. The filter thread is not modelled: a 24-sided lip (56 mm inside) and groove (60 mm) stand for it, deeper than a real 58 x 0.75 mm thread (about 57.2 and 58 mm), so the latches bite more than on the real lens. The cap is a plate, two fixed lugs and two sprung slider latches (2 N at 2.5 mm, est) with ramped teeth: latching is contact and springs, no rule. Cap, tab and lens-front sizes and the mass split are est.
reset_notes: Pinch the cap's tabs and take it off the lens; lay it face up at x 250 mm, y -130 mm. Stand the camera on its base with the lens toward the right arm, lens axis at x 340 mm, the lens's front face at y -30 mm (tape marks at the base's corners). Lens zoom at 18 mm (retracted), no hood, strap tucked under the body. Nothing is consumed; between trials check that both tabs spring back fully.
